problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- ${A}^{T}=A$
- ${A}^{2}=A$
- $A$ is an orthogonal projection matrix

activity_context.topic_title: Projection Matrices, Linear Transformations and Their Properties

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- ${A}^{T}=A$
- ${A}^{2}=A$
- $A$ is an orthogonal projection matrix
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that $Q$ is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if ${Q}^{2}=Q$ and ${Q}^{T}=Q.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, ${A}^{T}=A.$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}20 & 10 \\ 10 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true since both statements I and II are true.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."
